title: ML Precipitation Prediction Framework and CeilBench v1.0 evaluation protocol
description:
Open-source framework and evaluation protocol for monthly precipitation prediction in mountainous areas using hybrid deep learning. The archive contains the model implementations, the analysis scripts that produce every number and figure in the accompanying manuscript, and the per-seed metric files needed to recompute them.

Model families. ConvLSTM (baseline, bidirectional, residual and attention variants); Fourier Neural Operators (pure FNO and an FNO-ConvLSTM hybrid decoder); Graph Neural Networks with Temporal Attention (GNN-TAT) with GCN, GAT and GraphSAGE encoders; a state-space (Mamba) variant; and a Late Fusion Ridge meta-learner over ConvLSTM and GNN-TAT predictions.

Evaluation protocol (CeilBench v1.0). Five components, each with a released implementation: anchoring every architecture to zero-cost references (persistence, seasonal-naive, per-cell monthly climatology) scored on identical targets; a multi-seed feature-by-architecture factorial that separates architectural effect from initialisation variance; a decomposition of apparent ensemble gain into calibration and combination terms; a deseasonalised anomaly test; and spatially explicit diagnostics of the learned spatial prior.

Study area and results. Boyacá, Colombian Andes, on the CHIRPS-SRTM dataset (61×65 grid, 3,965 cells, 518 monthly steps, 1981–2024), seeds {42, 123, 456}, lead times H=1..12. The Late Fusion ensemble attains R²=0.655±0.018 across seeds. A per-cell monthly climatology attains R²=0.73 and is exceeded by no architecture, and the same anchoring step applied to eight further precipitation regimes returns a climatology ceiling between 0.548 and 0.899, so the ceiling is a property of the problem rather than of this region.

What is new in v1.2.0. The graph construction was corrected: inter-cell correlations are now estimated on the training period only, removing a target leakage, and the edge budget is an explicit hyperparameter rather than a constant behind a trigger. The training loop was instrumented, so compute cost is measured and recorded in the run metadata rather than estimated. New analysis scripts quantify the leakage (−0.002 in R², measured by a paired three-seed ablation), characterise the graph the model actually receives, rebuild the benchmark from per-seed files instead of best-seed values, and apply the anchoring step to eight regimes of global CHIRPS. A CPU smoke test extracts the training loop from the notebook and exercises it without a GPU.

Reference environment. Python 3.12.5, PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, PyTorch Geometric 2.7.0, CUDA 12.4. requirements-lock.txt pins every transitive dependency. Training measured on one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB.

Scope of this release. Archive accompanying the manuscript under submission to Geoscientific Model Development. It supersedes the earlier deposits, whose GNN-TAT results were produced with the leaked graph and reported as best-seed values; see models/provenance/investigation_headline_r2_2026-08-03.md in the archive for the full account of what changed and why.
